intentionally_empty.detail: All 7 acceptance criteria held at base 1f4974b (Proxy.handle already ran the D-050 order and threw plain HttpException 400/405/501 with a null message); test-only commit e1fa9d5, no implementation commit. Evidence: ProxyCheckOrderTest 9/9 green, each test red under a temporary reordering mutation.

declared_limits: The real total-timeout watchdog (JVM-wide lazy scheduler, D-066) and TOTAL_TIMEOUT belong to wave-18; only the package-private ProxyExchange.Watchdog/Reservation seam (no-op default) exists, reserved right after the slot and cancelled exactly once on release.

REL-PROXY-001 AC-2/AC-4: at this base a read timeout and a refused connect reach onError as HttpException(502), not ProxyException (READ_TIMEOUT/CONNECT_FAILED classification is wave-18); AC-2 tests accept either form, AC-4's ProxyException path uses a failed TLS handshake.

Core DefaultResponse.runTransfer calls ex.finish() before closing the relayed stream, so the slot outlives the last client byte briefly; fixing needs NaruServe-api (outside the write set). Tests poll the counter to 0.
TinyHttpd does not report an idle client disconnect while the relay is blocked reading a quiet backend; the slot is then held until the read timeout. Proxy documentation (wave-21) should state it.
FND-101 (record): ProxyExchangeTest.awaitBlockedRelayCopy scans every JVM thread for a blocked relay copy; it could fail falsely only if another test leaves a relay blocked (none does).
